description: Use this when the user wants a printable setlist for a gig or band (set list, stage setlist, setlist template, "print our set list", "how long is our set") as a PDF and CSV. Pass songs[] in play order with title and, when given, key, bpm, capo, duration ("3:45"), notes, segue and transpose; use sets[] when the sets are decided, or pass the pasted list as text (numbered lists, "Song - Key - BPM - Time", CSV or tab rows, "->" segues, SET 2 / Encore / --- breaks). Options: split_sets or break_after_minutes to split one list, changeover_seconds, transpose_all, band, venue, date, layout (both, stage, band) and paper (letter, a4). Returns set totals and the show total in m:ss; songs without a duration are listed and not estimated. Does not look up keys, tempos or song lengths, and does not make chord charts or lyrics.

band.description: Band or act name printed at the top. Example: The Late Shift

break_after_minutes.description: Start a new set when a set would run past this many minutes. Example: 45

changeover_seconds.description: Seconds between songs counted in the set times (none after a segue). Default 0. Example: 20

date.description: Gig date as it should print. Example: Sat 14 Nov 2026

layout.description: both (default: big-type stage pages plus a band copy table), stage, or band. Example: stage

songs.description: Songs of this set in order.

bpm.description: Tempo in beats per minute. Example: 150

capo.description: Capo fret for the guitarist (0 = none). Example: 2

duration.description: Length as m:ss, seconds or minutes: "3:45", 225, "3m45s", "3.5 min". Example: "3:05"

key.description: Key the band plays it in (sounding key). Example: G, Bb, F#m

notes.description: Short cue for the band. Example: count in 4, horns on chorus

segue.description: True when this song runs straight into the next one (no changeover). Example: true

set.description: Optional set name or number for this song; a change starts a new set. Example: "Set 2"

title.description: Song title. Example: Brown Eyed Girl

transpose.description: Change the key for this song: semitones (+2, -1) or a target key ("to A"). Example: "+2"

sets.description: Use instead of songs when the sets are already decided, e.g. [{"name":"Set 1","songs":[...]},{"name":"Encore","songs":[...]}].

bpm.description: Tempo in beats per minute. Example: 150

capo.description: Capo fret for the guitarist (0 = none). Example: 2

duration.description: Length as m:ss, seconds or minutes: "3:45", 225, "3m45s", "3.5 min". Example: "3:05"

key.description: Key the band plays it in (sounding key). Example: G, Bb, F#m

notes.description: Short cue for the band. Example: count in 4, horns on chorus

segue.description: True when this song runs straight into the next one (no changeover). Example: true

set.description: Optional set name or number for this song; a change starts a new set. Example: "Set 2"

title.description: Song title. Example: Brown Eyed Girl

transpose.description: Change the key for this song: semitones (+2, -1) or a target key ("to A"). Example: "+2"

songs.description: Songs in play order, one object per song, e.g. [{"title":"Valerie","key":"Eb","bpm":116,"duration":"3:40"}]. A plain string such as "SET 2" or "Encore" starts a new set. Up to 80 songs.

split_sets.description: Split a single list into this many sets of similar length, keeping the order (2 to 6). Example: 2

text.description: Fallback: the setlist as the user pasted it, one song per line, e.g. "1. Brown Eyed Girl (G) 150 bpm 3:05 capo 2\nSET 2\nValerie - Eb - 3:40 ->". Reads numbered lists, CSV or tab rows with a header, "->" segues and SET 2 / Encore / --- breaks.

transpose_all.description: Shift every song with a known key by these semitones or to a key name. Example: -2

venue.description: Venue printed at the top. Example: Blue Door Pub

name: generate_setlist
title: Generate a printable setlist
